description: Corresponding source for every copyleft (LGPL/GPL) component Keel ships, and the components compiled into shipped files that no lock file lists. Read by scripts/offline-compliance.sh (fetch and verify on the connected build machine) and by keel-sbom (SBOM and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES). Not legal advice; see docs/third-party/legal-review.md.

sources.purpose: Source at tag 0.0.23: the occt-import-js C++ wrapper, CMake files and the build scripts (tools/) used to compile the WebAssembly module. It references OpenCascade Technology as a git submodule, which this archive does not contain: see occt-source.

OpenCascade Technology at the commit that the occt submodule of occt-import-js tag 0.0.23 pins (gitlink d2abb6d844231cb8f29be6894440874a4700e4a5), including LICENSE_LGPL_21.txt and OCCT_LGPL_EXCEPTION.txt.

The npm package the two shipped files were copied from (dist/occt-import-js.js and dist/occt-import-js.wasm), so a recipient can compare the shipped bytes with the upstream build output. It also carries the wrapper source and the licence files.

bundled.name: OpenCascade Technology (OCCT)
bundled.note: Compiled into occt-import-js.wasm. The pinned revision comes from the occt submodule entry of occt-import-js 0.0.23.

bundled.name: Emscripten runtime libraries (Emscripten 3.1.69)
bundled.note: Status: unconfirmed. Listed because the files were built with Emscripten 3.1.69, whose runtime pieces (JavaScript glue, musl libc, libc++) are normally linked in. The binary was not inspected to confirm which of them it contains. Permissive licences only; no source offer is needed for them.

osLayers.statement: The container images (UBI 9 base of the application image, the PostgreSQL, SeaweedFS and Caddy images) contain Linux distribution packages under GPL and LGPL (for example glibc, bash, coreutils). Their corresponding source is distributed by the image publishers (Red Hat for UBI 9, the upstream projects for the others). Source archives of those packages are NOT in the bundle unless the release engineer passes --os-sources-dir to scripts/package-offline.sh. This is a recorded open item (docs/third-party/legal-review.md).
